CVE-2026-13506 (GHSA-qp49-qgx5-5m26): in Bouncy Castle, forcing a lazily parsed ASN.1 sequence resets the guard that limits how deeply nested input is parsed. For Bouncy Castle for Java FIPS, bc-fips 2.1.x before 2.1.3 is affected and 2.1.3 carries the fix; the advisory also lists the non-FIPS bcprov providers, which these packages do not ship: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qp49-qgx5-5m26, https://github.com/bcgit/bc-java/wiki/CVE%E2%80%902026%E2%80%9013506. The DHI eclipse-temurin-17-jdk packages for Alpine 3.23 ship Bouncy Castle FIPS in their eclipse-temurin-17-jdk-fips subpackage, as /usr/lib/bouncycastle/bc-fips-<version>.jar. Read the manifest of every jar in every published eclipse-temurin-17-jdk-fips package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine security repository (18 versions, 17.0.18.8-r0 to 17.0.21.9.1.2-r0; x86_64, and aarch64 for 17.0.18.8-r0 to 17.0.19.10-r6). The bc-fips jar is 2.1.2 in 17.0.18.8-r0 to 17.0.20.1.1-r0 and in 17.0.20.8-r0 and 17.0.20.8-r1, and 2.1.3 in 17.0.20.1.1-r1, and in 17.0.20.8.1.1-r2 and every later build. 17.0.20.8-r0 sorts after 17.0.20.1.1-r1 but went back to bc-fips 2.1.2, so the range closes at 17.0.20.1.1-r1, reopens at 17.0.20.8-r0 and closes again at 17.0.20.8.1.1-r2, the next build with 2.1.3. None of the eclipse-temurin-17-jdk, eclipse-temurin-17-jdk-oci-config or eclipse-temurin-17-jdk-fips-oci-config packages published for Alpine 3.23 contains a Bouncy Castle jar.
